title: Super Plot spec v1
description: A declarative chart: a chart type, tabular rows and the columns to encode. Limits: 50000 rows.

oneOf.title: Bar chart
oneOf.description: Compares a number across categories with one bar per category (grouped, stacked or 100% stacked). Comparing sizes across a handful to a few dozen categories, or parts of a whole per category (stacked). Use a line for ordered time; use a histogram to show how one measure is distributed; avoid for more than ~40 categories.

stack.description: `none` groups series side by side, `stack` stacks them, `normalize` stacks to 100%.

orientation.description: Use `horizontal` for long category names or many categories.

sort.description: Order categories by their total. `none` keeps the data order (use it for ordered categories such as months).

labels.description: Print values on the bars. Keep off for dense charts; the tooltip carries the numbers.

line.description: Combo chart: numeric column(s) drawn as lines with points over vertical bars, on the same value axis (a target, an average). Ignored for horizontal and 100% stacked bars. (column name, or several for wide-form data)

yScale.description: Only `linear`. A bar's length starts at zero, which a log axis cannot show, so `log` is refused (`log_scale_refused`). Use a line or a scatter for values spanning several orders of magnitude.

oneOf.title: Area chart
oneOf.description: A line chart with the area under it filled; stacked areas show how parts add up over time. Volume or cumulative quantity over time, and composition over time (`stack: "stack"` or `"normalize"`). Avoid overlapping unstacked areas for more than 2 series; use lines instead.

oneOf.description: Plots each row as a point by two numbers to show relationships, clusters and outliers; optional bubble size and trend line. Not for ordered time series (use line) or part-to-whole.

No expressions. E.g. [{"timeUnit":{"field":"date","unit":"month","as":"month"}},{"aggregate":{"groupBy":["month"],"fields":{"revenue":"mean"}}}]. Column fields then refer to the output.

patterns.description: Default false. Add a texture per series to filled marks (bars, areas, slices, cells) so series stay apart without colour: colour-blind readers, greyscale print.

geo.description: Optional boundaries drawn as land (needed when from/to name regions). The name of a geography registered with registerGeography (Super Plot ships none), or an inline GeoJSON FeatureCollection / TopoJSON Topology (key: feature id, else properties.id, else properties.name).

from.description: Origin region column (needs geo), or the origin's name when fromLat/fromLng are given. (name of a column in data)

to.description: Destination region column (needs geo), or the destination's name. (name of a column in data)

fromLat.description: Origin latitude column, degrees. (name of a column in data)

fromLng.description: Origin longitude column, degrees. (name of a column in data)

toLat.description: Destination latitude column, degrees. (name of a column in data)

toLng.description: Destination longitude column, degrees. (name of a column in data)

value.description: Numeric column giving each arc's width. (name of a column in data)

series.description: Column that colours arcs by group. (name of a column in data)

view.description: `flat`: a world projection fitted to the data (tilt it with camera.pitch). `globe`: a sphere the viewer can turn.

projection.description: Flat view only. `equal-earth` keeps areas true (best for comparing regions); `mercator` keeps shapes for zoomed-in maps.

camera.description: Starting view: {lng, lat} centre in degrees, zoom (1 fits the data), pitch (0-70 degrees of tilt, flat view) and bearing (degrees). The viewer can drag and zoom from there.

disputed.description: How to draw regions your geography marks as disputed: `same` as any other (no judgement), `dashed` outline, or `muted` fill with a dashed outline. Super Plot never decides what is disputed.

graticule.description: Draw meridians and parallels every 30 degrees. Default: on for the globe and for flat maps without geo, off otherwise.
